recipe.title: Bramley and rhubarb pots with hazelnut crunch
recipe.intro: Stored Bramleys are still going strong as the first pink rhubarb arrives, and together they make a soft, sharp compote that tastes like spring.
steps: Put the apples, rhubarb, orange zest and juice, sugar, cinnamon and water in a saucepan. Cover and cook over a low heat for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until the Bramleys collapse into a fluffy purée and the rhubarb is soft.
Take the pan off the heat and leave the compote to cool for about 20 minutes. It will thicken as it sits.
Meanwhile, toast the hazelnuts and pumpkin seeds in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking the pan, until golden and smelling nutty.
Add the butter, honey and a pinch of salt and stir for about a minute until everything is coated and sticky. Tip onto a plate and spread out to cool and crisp up.
Spoon the compote into four glasses or small bowls, top with the yoghurt and scatter over the hazelnut crunch just before eating.
recipe.tip: The compote keeps for 4 days in the fridge and freezes well, and the crunch stays crisp for a week in a jar.
